name: AI News
blurb: Daily AI news from the publishers who broke it, split into headline coverage of the field and vendor announcements from the companies building it. Every story links to the original source, and any claim quoted in our coverage is cross-referenced against the laws, lawsuits, companies, tools, papers, and people already tracked in this atlas.

domains.name: AI Headline News
domains.blurb: The day's most consequential AI stories across law, policy, research, safety, and society, curated from 34 vetted feeds. Each item carries the original publisher link and a note on how it connects to the bills, cases, and frameworks tracked elsewhere on this site.

domains.name: AI Vendor News
domains.blurb: Product launches, model releases, pricing changes, and company announcements from the AI vendors themselves. Each item links to the vendor's original announcement and cross-references the company's profile in our AI Companies directory where one exists.

domains.name: This Week in AI
domains.blurb: A weekly record of what moved in AI policy and litigation, permalinked by ISO week.

domains.name: AI Historical Timeline
domains.blurb: From the 1940s to the present: Turing, the perceptron, expert systems, backpropagation, deep learning, AlexNet, transformers, and what followed.

reading.body:
AI news coverage only matters if it tracks what actually moves the field. This atlas links 445 pages of daily AI stories to 34 vetted news feeds, then cross-references every claim against the laws, lawsuits, companies, and research already mapped here. That connection between news and verified fact is the filtering that separates signal from noise.

Most AI coverage lives in two separate worlds. Trade press announces what vendors want known. Policy outlets report what regulators do. This atlas pulls both into one system, so a reader sees when a product launch actually matters because it changes what a law affects, or when a lawsuit outcome reshapes what a company can build. The 445 headline pages and 1 vendor page show the ratio: regulation and research move slower than announcements, but both matter for understanding what constrains AI development.

The data covers news and policy. It does not cover real-time compute availability, power generation, or data center construction timelines. A reader looking here for whether the grid can actually support AI scaling will find the regulatory and legal facts that shape investment in that infrastructure, but not the engineering constraints themselves. That gap is the atlas working as designed: news and law are upstream of the physical limits they create.
